hormuz_disruption.label: Iran / Hormuz Disruption
hormuz_disruption.last_note: The 60-day ceasefire MOU is in force but PBS reporting from June 15 confirms Hormuz vessel traffic remains far below pre-war levels and the IEA states full restoration requires 6 to 8 months — disruption thesis is alive but the acute risk premium is partially priced out by the truce narrative, pushing WTI down to $75 from prior highs above $94.

stagflation_regime.label: Stagflation Regime
stagflation_regime.last_note: BLS May 2026 CPI confirmed at 4.2 percent YoY — highest since April 2023 — with Core CPI at 2.9 percent, PCE at 3.8 percent, and the Fed frozen at 3.50 to 3.75 percent under new Chair Warsh, delivering a textbook stagflationary policy trap.

ai_bubble_risk.label: AI Bubble Risk Q4 2026
ai_bubble_risk.last_note: Combined hyperscaler capex confirmed at $600 to $725 billion for 2026 with OpenAI spending roughly $60 billion annually against $13 billion in revenue, the Fed formally listing AI as a top systemic risk, and Morgan Stanley warning that the AI buildout now exceeds dot-com era telecom capex — monetization proof remains absent but capex shows no signs of deceleration, keeping the bubble risk elevated but not yet triggered.

gold_supercycle.label: Gold Supercycle
gold_supercycle.last_note: Gold has corrected from above $5,500 in January to $4,227 today — a drawdown exceeding 22 percent — but J.P. Morgan targets $6,000 by year-end, Bank of America forecasts a 2026 average of $4,538, and Goldman Sachs raised its end-2026 target to $5,400, confirming the supercycle thesis is intact structurally even as the current correction tests conviction.

copper_deficit.label: Structural Copper Deficit
copper_deficit.last_note: Goldman Sachs 2026 outlook confirms a structural ex-US refined copper deficit supporting an $11,400 per tonne price forecast, J.P. Morgan notes copper prices have been volatile since the Iran conflict but macro risks are not yet fully priced, and Trump 50 percent tariffs on copper imports have further tightened the US domestic supply picture.

nuclear_renaissance.label: Nuclear Renaissance
nuclear_renaissance.last_note: Contract offer bands have firmed to $86 to $90 per pound with Bank of America forecasting uranium prices rising 43 percent YoY to $105 per pound in H2 2026 as US utility buying returns, Cameco remains the top institutional pick, and IEA forecasts annual nuclear investment rising to $210 billion by the mid-2030s — the thesis is strengthening not weakening.

ALAB.note: Q1 2026 revenue of $308 million up 93 percent YoY confirms the AI connectivity thesis is intact operationally, but at P/E 99 the stock is priced for continued perfection and the AI bubble risk pillar at WATCH creates a valuation compression risk if capex narratives shift — next earnings catalyst is August 11, 2026.

POWL.note: The data center electrical infrastructure thesis remains supported by the hyperscaler capex supercycle but no new contract catalyst has emerged and the P/E of 43 leaves limited margin of safety if data center buildout timelines slip under macro pressure.

MOD.note: Negative FCF of minus $101 million remains a disqualifying quality flag — the original thermal management thesis has not improved to the point where capital discipline concerns can be set aside, and the Consumer Cyclical sector classification creates additional stagflation headwinds.

GFS.note: The CHIPS Act foundry thesis produces no new major contract catalyst and GlobalFoundries remains a laggard versus TSMC and Samsung in leading-edge nodes, with the stagflation regime compressing industrial semiconductor demand and no clear near-term revenue acceleration signal.

CRDO.note: FY2026 revenue of $1.34 billion up 205 percent with FY2027 guidance projecting over 80 percent revenue growth and optical products exceeding $600 million, plus the DustPhotonics acquisition expanding silicon photonics capabilities — the AI infrastructure connectivity thesis is the strongest in the reviewed cohort, but the analyst consensus price target of $256 is below the current price of $271, flagging near-term upside exhaustion.

ARM.note: ARM at P/E 143 with only $750 million FCF remains priced for absolute perfection with no margin of safety — the royalty model is a long-duration asset that is disproportionately vulnerable to the 10-year yield at 4.45 percent and any AI capex deceleration would compress the data center licensing growth narrative that justifies the multiple.

S.note: SentinelOne crossed $1 billion in annual revenue with 22 percent YoY growth and achieved first-ever full-year operating profitability, but the May layoff of 8 percent of headcount and lackluster forward guidance signals the company is sacrificing near-term growth for margin — at $15 the stock trades at 3.5x NTM EV to revenue, cheap relative to CRWD but the growth deceleration versus CrowdStrike is a thesis drift risk.

ZS.note: Zscaler maintains the strongest FCF in cybersecurity at $1.1B but remains rated AVOID — the valuation at P/E 28.37 does not screen as expensive yet the growth deceleration thesis and intensifying platform competition have not resolved in ZS favor.

AXON.note: AXON at EV-to-EBITDA 379 with only $63 million FCF represents complete thesis drift from a law enforcement hardware play to an overvalued SaaS narrative — no new catalysts have emerged to justify the multiple and the original public safety infrastructure thesis has been fully overwhelmed by speculative premium.

ISRG.note: Intuitive Surgical has zero debt, $4.5B cash, 23% revenue growth, and $2.3B FCF making it a genuine compounder, but at 36x forward earnings and 29.4% below highs the surgical robotics moat thesis is unchanged — the drift is purely valuation-related, not fundamental, and the stock remains a hold-not-add until the multiple contracts further.

RXRX.note: Recursion Pharmaceuticals has revenue growth of minus 56.1%, is burning $178M in FCF with negative operating margins of minus 1985%, and is 55.2% below its 52-week high — the original AI drug discovery thesis has collapsed as clinical pipeline progress has not justified the technology premium and this is now a capital destruction story with no near-term catalyst.

JEDI.note: The drone and modern warfare rearmament thesis is structurally intact given the Hormuz crisis has accelerated defense technology procurement, but at 25% below highs and with no fundamental data available for an ETF wrapper this remains a theme trade that requires a defined technical base before adding risk.

CWAN.note: Clearwater Analytics has 74.4% revenue growth and $160M FCF which is operationally compelling, but analyst targets of $24.47 to $24.55 against the current $24.35 price provide virtually zero upside consensus — at PEG of 10.24 and EV/EBITDA of 73.69 the institutional fintech thesis is fully priced with no margin of safety.

GRAB.note: Grab at $3.30 with $6.5B cash, 23.5% revenue growth, and PEG of 0.87 is the most asymmetric deep value setup in the portfolio on a pure fundamentals basis, but the stock is 50.2% below highs and the Southeast Asia super-app monetization thesis requires a specific catalyst such as a buyback announcement or profitability upgrade to unlock value — thesis intact, no trigger yet.

VRT.note: Vertiv is a direct beneficiary of the above 1 trillion dollar 2026 data center capex cycle with power constraint urgency confirmed by the Microsoft 80 billion dollar Azure backlog, but stretched valuation demands flawless execution at a time when macro uncertainty is high.

MU.note: MU led the chip stock rally on June 15 on Iran deal optimism and structural AI memory demand is intact given that memory cost inflation drove data center capex higher in Q1 2026, but the stock is cyclical and a stagflation-driven consumer slowdown could compress DRAM pricing outside the AI data center vertical.

AMD.note: AMD surged on June 15 following an analyst upgrade and the Iran deal catalyst, with the company announcing up to 2 billion pounds in UK AI investment and the MEXT memory optimization acquisition signaling a serious data center strategy, but the stock at 548.80 dollars trades at a premium that assumes continued hyperscaler GPU wallet share gains from Nvidia.
